children: was in the spotlight on Friday as HSBC upgraded the electronic design automation firm, citing its potential from artificial intelligence.

“New business model to transform Synopsys from a slow-growth software play to a high-growth AI beneficiary,” HSBC analyst Frank Lee wrote in a note to clients. “Design IP licensing-plus-royalty model and agentic AI integration in EDA to drive earnings upside, help re-rate.”
Lee raised his rating on Synopsys to Buy from Hold and upped his price target to $700 from $490.

Delving deeper, Lee said Synopsys has moved from a strategy where it implements “build once, sell many” to one of deeper collaboration with semiconductor companies and can provide custom silicon solutions.

“It shifts Synopsys up the value chain by combining licensing revenue with royalties,” Lee explained. “We believe this will give Synopsys a lot more scale and increase its TAM, as revenue becomes linked to chip volumes. This model would be targeted for customers such as hyperscalers, ASIC vendors or foundries. We expect the royalty revenue to be highly margin accretive and drive earnings growth significantly.”

He continued: “We expect agentic AI to drive a fundamental shift in the EDA business model – EDA tools will move from assisting engineers to AI agents managing the entire workflows on its own. Synopsys is now exploring a shift from traditional subscription licenses for human engineers to subscription-plus-consumption models for agents. This transition could lead to enhanced revenue as these agents could take on more engineering work and orchestrate the underlying EDA tools at a significantly higher rate.”

title: Synopsys in spotlight as HSBC upgrades on AI prospects
